text:
lisa-ng: Heads up — onboarding a new Dedicated GPU customer next week and we're hitting networking limits when we smoke-test the fleet. Need to open a quota request with AWS for a few things across us-west-2 and eu-west-1.

omar-khan: Can you itemize what exactly we need? numbers + rationale helps the support case.

lisa-ng: Sure. TL;DR: 500 new GPU nodes (p4d/p4de-like), expect 200 concurrent boot bursts during scale tests. We need: increase Elastic IPs (EIP) per region from 50 -> 250, increase per-instance ENI attach limit for the instance family to support 8 secondary ENIs per GPU VM, bump account ENI quota from 2000 -> 8000, and request a /56 IPv6 prefix per VPC for dual-stack to avoid IPv4 private IP exhaustion. Also we want a NAT gateway port quota review because ephemeral ports were a bottleneck in load-testing.

rahul_m: Adding context — our autoscaler launches many short-lived spot-backed worker pods. Each GPU VM attaches a network ENI for tenant isolation and an extra ENI for load-balancer health checks. With current ENI limit we start failing instance launches once we hit ~180 active nodes.

omar-khan: Do we have exact numbers of expected ENIs per node? you said 8 secondary but can you break down?

lisa-ng: Breakdown per GPU instance (expected): 1 primary ENI (eth0), 2 per-tenant ENIs (avg 3 tenants/node for multitenant testing) -> ~3 secondary, 1 ENI for monitoring/agent, 1 ENI for public egress (EIP role), 1 additional ENI reserved for future LB/sidecar. Peak config = 7 ENIs per instance. We're asking for safe headroom at 8 secondary per instance to account for burst tests.

marie-prod: Why EIPs? can these be NATed from a smaller pool? customers need stable public endpoints for license callbacks and webhooks — they verify IP allowlists. We need persistent EIPs for certain VMs.

lisa-ng: Correct. Persistent EIPs required for license webhook and some legacy integrations. NAT gateway only helps for outbound but we still need dedicated public addresses for inbound callbacks and third-party allowlists.

aws-support-bot: AWS case opened: 123456789012345. Summary: Increase EIP quota to 250, ENI-per-instance limit for Accelerated-compute family, account ENI quota to 8000, assign /56 IPv6 prefix to VPCs in us-west-2 and eu-west-1, review NAT gateway port quotas. Case link: https://console.aws.amazon.com/support/cases#/case/?caseId=123456789012345

omar-khan: Nice. Please paste the exact rationale blob I can forward to the AWS TAM and also include expected timeline and cost ack.

lisa-ng: Pasted rationale below (send to AWS TAM):

```
Customer onboarding for Redwood Dedicated GPU pool. Deployment plan: 2 initial Dedicated pools (us-west-2, eu-west-1) intended to host 500 GPU worker VMs each across multiple AZs. Expected concurrent boot bursts up to 200 nodes during testing and up to 500 under customer acceptance testing. Networking design assigns multiple ENIs per VM for tenant isolation, monitoring, and public endpoints. Without increased EIP and ENI quotas we observe failed instance attachments and inability to provision IPs for new VMs, causing provisioning failures and missed SLAs. IPv6 /56 allocation requested per VPC to enable dual-stack addressing and reduce dependency on scarce IPv4 private ranges. Please approve quota increases or advise on alternative approaches (Elastic IP pool reservations, prefix delegation) to support production Dedicated fleet onboarding. Priority: high. Contact: lisa-ng@redwood.com, infra lead: omar-khan@redwood.com.
```

rahul_m: Also include expected retention of EIPs — we'll tag and release unused ones after 30 days of idle state. Add cost acknowledgement — we're aware of public IPv4 scarcity charges and will accept per-address costs.

lisa-ng: Added note in the case.

omar-khan: We should also ask for a soft limit increase review for AWS-managed NAT gateway concurrent port allocation. During load tests we hit ephemeral port exhaustion leading to 502s outbound. If AWS can't increase NAT port limits, ask for guidance on scaling NAT (multiple NAT gateways / per-AZ) or use EIP per-node as fallback.

sre-oncall: FYI — will monitor CloudWatch alarms for ENI::AllocateAddress failures and AutoScaling Launch failures. I put a temp alert dashboard.

aws-support-bot: Update on case 123456789012345: Initial reply from AWS TAM requests exact account IDs and VPC IDs and to confirm which subnets require the /56 IPv6 delegation. They also asked to confirm whether we're using ClassicLink (we're not) and requested justification for per-instance ENI increase specific to the accelerated compute instance family.

lisa-ng: Replying with account and VPC IDs now. Omar — can you dump the VPC list and a sample subnet ID for us-west-2?

omar-khan: Pasting sample: vpc-0a1b2c3d4e5f6g7h (us-west-2), subnets: subnet-0aa111bb, subnet-0aa222cc. Will attach the full list to the support case.

rahul_m: One more ask: request we get a temporary quota bump with a 30-day review instead of a permanent change while we validate usage patterns. That usually speeds AWS approval.

lisa-ng: Good call — updated case to request a 30-day trial increase then revert to measured limits.

marie-prod: Can infra estimate monthly cost delta for the increased EIP/ENI headroom so finance can pre-approve?

omar-khan: Rough ballpark: additional EIPs 200 * $3.5/mo = ~$700/mo. ENI objects are free but potentially increase NAT/elastic network resource usage; estimate extra egress NAT charges ~$1k–2k/mo based on current traffic estimates. We'll refine after 30-day trial.

sre-oncall: I'll add temporary dashboarding and tag rules so we can sweep idle EIPs weekly.

aws-support-bot: Case update: TAM assigned (TAM ID: TAM-908172). They scheduled a call for 2026-04-01 17:00 UTC to review technical details. Please prepare network diagrams and the autoscaler launch pattern.

lisa-ng: Thanks — I'll prep the diagram and share in this thread. For now, if anyone has objections to the 30-day trial bump, raise them here. Otherwise I'll finalize the support case with account/VPC details. :thumbsup:

omar-khan: No objections. Approve.

marie-prod: Approve from product side.

rahul_m: Approve from ML infra.

sre-oncall: Approve and will take on monitoring after approval.

lisa-ng: Filed and updated. Will post the AWS case thread updates here.

aws-support-bot: Case 123456789012345 status: Awaiting TAM call.

lisa-ng: Thread closed for now — follow-up after TAM sync.
